text: Most guys get this wrong. Let's talk about relationships versus a popular term today, situationships. For a lot of the guys, the very first woman who likes them back, that's it. They're ready to lock it in, build a relationship, and imagine a future together. Why? Because deep down they could be afraid they won't find another girl or they think that this is what they're supposed to do. To show their friends and society, look, I've got a partner, I made it. But here's the problem. Is she or he himself even good for a relationship? Most guys don't stop to ask that. They just think, we'll figure it out, we'll make it work. Criteria? None. And since they barely have any experience, where would those criteria even come from? Movies, TV shows, love songs, all selling the same lie that any relationship can work if you just try hard enough. Wrong. Here's some statistics. Most marriages end in divorce. Relationships? Here's statistics is even worse. Because a good relationship isn't just being together. At its core, it's consensual exclusivity. You both choose each other. And for that to work, you need clear standards based on your own experience. What you like, what you don't like, what you can handle, what you cannot handle. And the reality is, only a small percentage of women and men are truly fit for healthy relationships. So how do you know if this girl or you yourself are one of them if you've never had enough experience? That's where situationships can play a role. Here you meet, you spend time together, you get close, but without big promises. If you see that this is the right person, you can try something more serious. If not, you can be honest and move on. Still, you need to be responsible. Because in situationships, one person almost always starts catching deeper feelings. And when that happens, you need the honesty to end it. Don't drag it out, no false promises, no lies. This way, you stay honest with yourself and with her. So don't rush. To build good relationships, you need right criteria and experience. And here's where situationships can help you. Understand what works and what doesn't work for you. Learn, and with that, when the right person comes, you'll know.
